subject.title: contextPruning (mode: cache-ttl) never fires on OpenAI models: isCacheTtlEligibleProvider excludes OpenAI, so the idle-gap tool-result firebreak is dead for the highest-volume provider

question: Should native OpenAI support for stale-tool-result pruning be implemented by widening the existing cache-TTL eligibility gate, or by adding a provider-agnostic pruning mode that does not depend on prompt-cache eligibility?
rationale: Both paths can address the report, but widening the current gate changes upgrade/session behavior for existing OpenAI configurations and needs maintainer intent before merge.

options.title: Approve OpenAI cache-TTL semantics with proof
options.body: Keep the linked PR path, require redacted native OpenAI idle-gap evidence, and explicitly accept or adjust the TTL/session behavior before merge.

options.title: Require provider-agnostic pruning
options.body: Ask for a replacement design that prunes stale tool results without treating native OpenAI as cache-TTL eligible.

options.title: Leave OpenAI ineligible
options.body: Close the linked PR direction and document that cache-TTL pruning remains limited to providers with approved cache semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve OpenAI cache-TTL semantics with proof
recommendation.body: Keep the linked PR path, require redacted native OpenAI idle-gap evidence, and explicitly accept or adjust the TTL/session behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest shipped cache-TTL helper state is tied to Vincent Koc's release commit, making him a practical routing candidate for the provider/session semantics decision.
